productionPolicy.instruction: Prioritize the next renderable scene or shot. Apply the responsible skills once to the bounded scene, retain decisions in Studio contracts, and reuse unchanged approved plans, references, workflows and jobs. Complete planning, required assets and prompts in one working pass without intermediate creative approval requests. Read only necessary skill references; do not reopen completed stages or create extra reports. A technical retry or prompt correction with the same directed Shot does not require a new shot plan. Replan only changed action, camera, duration, routing or dependencies. Story changes require a Screenwriting revision. Board creation is optional: generate a missing individual composed frame directly using relevant approved references and continuity anchors. Send each ready authorized shot before preparing unrelated scenes. Register its remote ID and return control; audiovisual review may remain pending.
safeguards: Preserve approved script and dependency lineage.
Use real required references and verified adapter limits.
Keep scoped resource authorization and human approval of paid spending.
Never resubmit uncertain jobs or modify master workflows.
No music; no audiovisual approval without viewing and listening.

hybridDirection.instruction: Read this local routing policy before directing shots, preparing assets, compiling prompts or reviewing video. It overrides vendor I2V-default and mandatory-board assumptions. Choose generationMode and routingReason per scene sequence: ltx_i2v for controlled composition, dialogue and subtle reactions; h3_reference_to_video with workflow H3_motion_ref2v for reference-driven physical action and coordinated movement. Route according to actual verified capabilities, never a whole-episode blanket choice. H3 uses an ordered Reference Plan, not a storyboard per cinematic shot. Respect the registered workflow’s verified per-video maximum and native frame alignment; split longer sequences into units that reuse references. A first-frame image is valid among the references: use role start and map its Picture label to the target opening at 0.00 seconds. One Studio Shot may hold a multi-shot H3 generation unit with contiguous timed shots; preserve approved source beats and dialogue once. LTX retains composed first frames and reusable conversation coverage. No render authorization is implied.

plan.retentionAnalysis: Keep Molly, Nick and Ethan visually distinct and stable across every cut. Favor close-ups and expressive listening reactions. At the boundary beat, Ethan's step toward Molly and Nick is clearly shown; cut to Molly looking directly at Ethan over his visible gray-suited shoulder as she speaks. Nick is farther back, visibly secondary. Molly pulls away from Nick; both men stop and give her space.
continuityRequirements: Lock the three approved faces and hairstyles to their identity references across every internal cut and both video units.
Molly and Nick begin beside each other at the bed; Ethan begins beside the chair; the doorway stays clear.
Preserve all three wedding outfits; Molly remains in the emerald-green dress.
Use simple American English, spoken slowly, clearly and naturally with expressive but restrained delivery; one speaker at a time. Exact source lines once only.
No captions, text, extra narration, improvised dialogue, extra gestures or music.
plan.expectedOutput: One 19.333-second vertical video with 7 close/medium-close compositions, including a dedicated Ethan step-in shot and Molly speaking to Ethan over his identifiable shoulder, with clean hard cuts.

Confirm Molly pulls away from Nick; Ethan freezes and Nick draws back.
Confirm no music, score, sting or added synthetic audio from first frame through last.

shotPlanningContract.prerequisite: Approved, skill-directed Studio Shot records from plan-camera-shots.

imageContinuityContract.appliesTo: LTX and other composed-frame routes only; exclude H3 reference generation
imageContinuityContract.workflow: Reuse compatible reviewed composed frames first. For missing compositions, generate only the individual frame needed from approved identity, location and wardrobe references plus the directed Shot. Maintain axis, eyelines, prop state and lighting. A scene board is optional when it solves a concrete continuity problem; it is never an I2V start frame.
imageContinuityContract.derivation: Create only missing distinct compositions as individual images. Include relevant approved references and the Shot continuity instructions; include a reviewed board only if one exists and is useful. Inspect each full image before attachment.
imageContinuityContract.persistence: If a scene board is created, save it under the production references/boards folder with episode and scene IDs. Save each single-shot image as that shot’s start-frame candidate, inspect it, then attach and approve it through the normal references workflow. Never substitute the multi-panel board for an I2V start frame.
imageContinuityContract.imageRequest: Include scene and shot IDs, shot order, framing, camera position, blocking, frozen action moment, continuity anchors, and reference roles in image requests. Keep static composition instructions separate from video motion.

shotPlanningContract.instruction: Compile only the approved shot plan. Do not derive, redesign, split, merge, or silently correct shots in this stage. Follow imageContinuityContract for composed frames; its mandatory flag determines whether a board is required. Reuse compatible existing compositions. For H3, compile its approved Reference Plan with ordered reference roles and subject mappings into the official six-section reference prompt, with explicit timed HARD CUTS where planned; do not request a board or image per cinematic shot and do not impose LTX continuous-shot restrictions. Video prompts must be production-ready and sufficiently descriptive: state scene context, visible subjects and stable identity anchors, composition, blocking, one dominant action progression per cinematic shot, performance change, camera behavior, start/end state, continuity and sound. Include the assigned duration in seconds and direct the model to complete only the planned action within that duration; do not add dead air, filler action, or unmotivated holds. Render all source action as narrative prose, never as screenplay dialogue blocks or character-name speaker labels. Render each exact spoken line once in quotation marks, attributed in prose to its speaker; tell the model to speak only quoted text and never vocalize names or narration. Require diegetic-only audio from the first frame to the last: no musical intro or outro, background score, reveal sting, suspense drone, riser, tonal pulse, bass drop, trailer boom, or synthetic impact accent. Do not add music from in-scene devices. Preserve natural quiet where no dialogue or planned sound occurs. Put this rule at the beginning and remind it at the end; include it in supported negative prompts. If direction is incomplete, return to task --stage shots. If only references or technical preflight are missing, resolve those without reopening an unchanged approved shot plan.

bible.premise: A celebrity reporter turns difficult experiences into entertaining stories, until she must face what those stories conceal.

approvedStoryAdapter.note: Replaces shape-story-blueprint with approved facts. These skill docs are methodological inputs; normalize results to studio schemas rather than maintaining a second editable project.

sceneSimplicity.instruction: Flag avoidable physical complexity when simpler staging could preserve the dramatic function. Do not impose quotas or simplify essential spectacle, choices or evidence away. Camera/coverage can be refined within approved facts; changes to entrances, concealment, actions, discoveries or consequences must return as recommendations to Screenwriting, never be silently rewritten in production.

wardrobeDirection.instruction: Separate character identity from clothing. An identity/reference sheet fixes stable face, hair and build, not a universal outfit. For each scene, choose context-appropriate clothing when clear (e.g. wedding attire at a wedding, swimwear at a pool), unless the screenplay or an approved scene-specific wardrobe reference establishes another deliberate choice. Treat unstated costume as a visual proposal, preserve it across the scene, and link any wardrobe asset/reference only to the relevant scenes and shots. Never rewrite the approved script or propagate a temporary outfit into identity.
